3. Decide what size blocks to use for each pattern. Common dimensions range from 0.5 to 5 feet, though a bigger or smaller dimension could suit your project's scale and budget.
4. Decide how many blocks per course (width x length) you'll stack. This relates to how tight the arrangement is and influences how thick and robust it will be.

2. Lay out the pattern blocks. Arrange them in the order determined during your initial planning sessions, ensuring that they fit seamlessly into the grid.
3. Use tape measures to verify that each set of blocks align neatly against the outer rim of each dimension marked.
